**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/20 (Sat) 23:44
- [USER] User expressed frustration about documentaries being biased and presenting only one side of an issue.
- [USER] User wishes documentaries would be more transparent about their biases.
- [USER] User feels that filmmakers do not trust people to make their own decisions.
- [USER] User wishes filmmakers would stop trying to push their own agendas and just let the facts speak for themselves.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Documentaries are meant to educate, inform, and raise awareness about a particular subject or issue.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Common underlying themes in documentaries include advocacy, education, awareness, empathy, and inspiration.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Documentaries can be biased as filmmakers have their own perspectives and may present information that supports their beliefs.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Some documentaries strive to present a balanced viewpoint while others may be one-sided and exclude opposing viewpoints.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is important to critically analyze and evaluate the content of documentaries before accepting them as factual and unbiased sources.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested ways to evaluate the balance of a documentary include checking sources, looking for counterarguments, evaluating the use of statistics and data, considering the tone, and doing additional research.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Documentarians bring their own experiences, biases, and beliefs to their work, which can affect how they communicate about the world.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Filmmakers may feel their point of view is necessary to be heard, especially on topics they feel have been overlooked.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Funding, distribution, and marketing pressures can influence filmmakers to take a particular perspective.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Transparency is crucial for helping viewers understand the perspective and agenda of the documentary filmmaker.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Some documentaries present disclaimers outlining their perspective and intention, but this is not always the case.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Viewers should take responsibility for doing their own research and seeking out different perspectives.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Documentaries can be a powerful tool to raise awareness and promote social change, but they should be approached with a critical mindset.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Filmmakers have their own subjectivity and perspective that informs the story they are telling, and it is not always possible to present an objective view.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Both filmmakers and viewers have a responsibility to engage with documentary content in a way that promotes transparency, accountability, and critical thinking.
